questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. "So, no good coming here with highfalutin ideas," he continued.

B. "There's one thing you must understand," said Edward to the housekeeper.

C. The housekeeper bowed and simply nodded in agreement.

D. "Just because we live in a big house doesn't mean we're rich!"
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BDAC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence B is the independent sentence and acts as an opening dialogue. It states how the housekeeper needs to understand one important thing. 
 
• So, sentence B is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• Sentence D states Edward's next speech which explains the one thing that the housekeeper needed to understand. Hence, D follows B.__
 
• Sentence **D **points out how even though Edward (and others) lived in a big house, it did not mean that they were rich. 
 
• Sentence A states the outcome of not being rich. It mentions how Edward states that as they are not rich the housekeeper should not come to them with highfalutin (pretentious) ideas. So, sentence **A** should come after sentence D, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence C is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides the housekeeper's reaction to Edward's statements. 
 
• Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 1 i.e. BDAC.

*So, the correct paragraph is : (B)**"There's one thing you must understand," said Edward to the housekeeper. (D) "Just because we live in a big house doesn't mean we're rich!" (A) "So, no good coming here with highfalutin ideas," he continued. (C) The housekeeper bowed and simply nodded in agreement.***

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

A lenient view of her case was taken by the judge.

options.text: The judge will take a lenient view of her case.
The judge has taken a lenient view of her case.
The judge took a lenient view of her case.
The judge takes a lenient view of her case.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The judge took a lenient view of her case.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in passive voice. As per the question we have to change it into active voice.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case) + was + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
• Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *A garden was built by her. (Passive voice)*
 
• *She built a garden. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject (objective case) of the given sentence is ‘**a lenient view of **her case’.
 
• The object (subjective case) of the given sentence is ‘the judge’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• was taken will be changed to took.

*Correct sentence - The judge took a lenient view of her case.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

I asked my mother where she kept the grocery.

options.text: I said to my mother, "Where have you kept the grocery?"
I said to my mother, "Where do you keep the grocery?"
I said to my mother, "Where does she keeps the grocery?"
I said to my mother, "Where she keeps the grocery?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**I said to my mother, "Where do you keep the grocery?**""

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in indirect speech and we need to convert it to direct speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to direct speech, we use the following rules - 
 
 
• The reporting verb asked is changed to said to. 
 
• The conjunction that is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech. 
 
• A comma (,) is added before the direct speech part. 
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in *capital letter. *
 
• The **past tense** kept is changed to its present tense form keep. 
 
• The pronoun she is changed from second person to first person you. 
 
• Since, the reported speech is a question, the verb do is added.
 
 
 
• So, by following the above rules, we get the direct speech as - I said to my mother, "Where do you keep the grocery?"
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

He has been given a notice to vacate the house.

options.text: We are giving him a notice to vacate the house.
We had given him a notice to vacate the house.
We gave him a notice to vacate the house.
We have given him a notice to vacate the house.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**We have given him a notice to vacate the house.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in passive voice. As per the question we have to change it into active voice.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case) + has been + past participle + *implied *by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
• Subject + have + past participle + Object (Active voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *He has been taken out by me. (Passive voice)*
 
• *I have taken him out. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject (objective case) of the given sentence is ‘**he**’.
 
• The object (subjective case) of the given sentence is implied - ‘by us’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• has been given will be changed to have given.

*Correct sentence - We have given him a notice to vacate the house.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

The tin-roofed house __gave up__ during the terrible storm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'gave way'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There is a **phrasal verb** error in the underlined part.
 
• **Gave up **is a phrasal verb of **"give"** which means **to cease making an effort or to admit defeat**. This does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• The meaning of the other options - 
 
 
• **Gave away - **give something freely as a gift or donation.
 
 
• *Example *- *I **gave away** all my books.*
 
 
 
• **Gave way - **(of a support or structure) be unable to carry a load or withstand a force; collapse or break.
 
 
• *Example *- *His aching legs **gave way**, and he almost fell.*
 
 
 
• **Gave over - **allow oneself to be taken over by emotion or addiction. 
 
 
• *Example - I **gave myself over** to the joy of gliding down a long ski run.*
 
 
 
 
 
• From the above meanings, it is clear that "**gave way" **will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. 
 
• Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

 

**Correct sentence__* - ****The tin-roofed house **__gave way__** during the terrible storm.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

The police officer said to him, "Why were you out till late last night?"

options.text: The police officer asked him that why he were out till late the previous night
The police officer asked him why he had been out till late the previous night.
The police officer asked him why had he been out till late last night.
The police officer asked him why was he out till late last night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The police officer asked him why he had been out till late the previous night.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is indirect speech. According to the question, we need to change it into indirect speech.
 
• The given speech is an interrogative sentence, where the police officer asks a question.
 
• The process of changing direct speech to its indirect form is as follows - 
 
 
• Since it is not a *yes-no question,*the reported speech will start with why.
 
• The reporting verb said is changed into asked or enquired. 
 
• The second person 'you' will be changed into he.
 
• The **past continuous tense **were changes to **past perfect continuous **had been in reported speech. 
 
• **'Last night' **becomes **'the previous night'**.
 
 
 
• ​Eventually, we will get the final sentence- The police officer asked him why he had been out till late the previous night.
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Nelson left his home / and went / to the sea / at an early age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'to the sea'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part is '**to the sea'.**
 
• In this segment, using the** definite article 'the'** before the **common noun sea **is incorrect. 
 
• **"Go to sea" **is a phrase of** 'sea' **that means **set out on a voyage; become a sailor in a navy or a merchant navy.**
 
• **For Examples:-**
 
 
• The fishermen were unable to** go to sea** in such storms.
 
• Garret left the small family farm in his late teens and **went to sea.**
 
 
 
• To make the sentence correct, we need to eliminate '**the'.**

 

***Correct sentence__ - ****Nelson left his home / and went / **to sea** / at an early age.*
